notice: Independent. Not affiliated with Open Standard or Bridge.

verdict.text: Local preview, not a finding. On Tempo and Ethereum, which hold about 98% of OUSD, 73% of supply has sat still for at least 14 days in unlabeled wallets of $1M or more, and transfers under $1M moved $45.5M in the last week, 0.35% of supply.
estimates: The figures cover Tempo and Ethereum and end on 2026-11-03, UTC.
Total supply on these chains is $12.8B, and each chain's mints minus burns equal its reported supply to the base unit.
About 98% of OUSD is on Tempo and Ethereum: end-of-day balances against the issuer's newest reported total, so this is approximate.
Placed supply is 73.43% of supply on these chains. It counts wallets with no public label, so an unlabeled issuer or venue wallet can count as placed.
Seven-day everyday volume is 0.35% of supply on these chains. It leaves out flows to and from labeled wallets, so a missing label adds to it.
opinions: So far this reads mostly like balance-sheet supply. The chain can't show why balances stay put.

known_limits.text: This is not a reserve attestation. It reads chain data and says nothing about the reserves. See Bridge's own reports for those.
Placed supply measures dollars that stayed in a wallet. It doesn't show why they stayed, and the chain can't show intent.
Everyday volume means clean transfers under $1M, nothing more. A payment can't be told from a bot or a treasury sweep.
Clean volume nets each transaction, but a chain of transfers across several transactions counts at every hop, so it can overstate.
Active wallets count wallets, not people.
Issuer inventory and venue supply count only wallets a public source labels. Unlabeled custody isn't counted as a venue, and can count as placed.
Day 0 was 2026-09-30, so this is weeks of history: a direction at most, not a trend.

Velocity divides clean volume by circulating supply, and headline velocity divides all volume by total supply. Circulating supply is smaller, so velocity can exceed headline velocity. Both denominators are published beside them.
Each chain stops at its own last complete UTC day, so chains can end on different days. A chain's KPIs end on its last day with a transfer, and each row names its day.
A transfer lost between two wallets, with no later rows, passes until one of them is drawn into a balance sample. On Tempo that is about 3% a run.
An error in Bridge's total that exactly equals the moves inside the comparison window matches one of the attainable sums.
Reorg repair is tested with simulated reorgs. Solana reads finalized data only, so it has no reorg test.
Solana has no wallet labeled as the issuer. Its issuer inventory counts only unnamed redemption-route wallets, if any, so it may be understated.
This is a local preview, never a release. It may leave out chains and checks.
Base and Solana is not covered by this local preview, and the full reconciliation was not checked.
